text:
Martin Pospisil plays like he has something to prove, and lately he's been proving it. The Flames' 2018 fourth-rounder has 95 hits in 20 games, eight points, and six of those in his last ten. A Calgary Herald column on Nov. 5 lumped him with Adam Klapka as proof that Craig Conroy's patience is paying off.

The points are running a bit hot. Over his last ten games his line has scored more than its chances would suggest, and his 1.77 points per 60 sits above our talent range's middle. His own shooting (10.3%) is right where it should be, though, and his chance rate is up from last season. At five on five he's neutral, a 47% expected goals share with the team about the same without him.

He's fast (91st percentile for bursts over 20 mph) and he hits everything, which can cut both ways: Markerzone ran the clip of Brandon Montour making him pay after a Seattle goalie got run over. Evolving-Hockey's note from his short 2025-26 sample is worth remembering: weak linemates, the other team's best players. Watch whether his minutes grow as Calgary trusts him with more.
